To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Wu <emily.wu@atlashealth.com>

Subject: QBR readout prep — infra runway, GPU spend, batching/caching trade-offs

Team —

We need a tight package for next week’s QBR: leadership wants a 5-slide readout that explains runway risk for infra, current GPU spend and utilization, and clear quantification of batching + caching levers (cost savings vs. tail-latency/regression risk). High-level asks below; I’ve attached a request worksheet.

Asks (one-pager + backup tables by EOD Friday 2/5):
- Snapshot: trailing-90d GPU spend by cluster/model family, and committed reserved spend vs. usage.
- Utilization: effective utilization by pool (prod, staging, non-prod) with current autoscale headroom.
- Levers: estimated token/cost savings from current batching/caching configs (median batch size, cache hit-rate, average prefix reuse). Include a scenario table: baseline, +20% batching, +cache TTL increase (30/60/90s).
- Risks: tail-latency impact estimates (p95/p99) and ops complexity for each lever.
- Executive ask: what’s the minimum committed capacity to maintain SLA for top-5 customers if we pull non-prod reserve by 15%?

Attachments: QBR_infra_runway_request_20270202.xlsx (worksheet), gpu_utilization_by_cluster_202701.pdf, batching_cache_sensitivity_v1.csv

Quick notes on formatting: one slide with the three charts (spend runway, utilization heatmap, lever sensitivity), appendix tables for simulation assumptions. Vivek — can you take the modeling? Lauren — please add the leadership framing and askline. Monica — round up any CS commitments and customer-specific SLAs that matter for the ask. Rishi — FYI / escalation path if runway looks tight. Emily — tagging since Atlas is in our top-5 by token volume; feel free to ignore if this is internal-only.

Thanks —
Kimberly

--

Subject: Re: QBR readout prep — infra runway, GPU spend, batching/caching trade-offs

Kimberly —

Quick pass from the infra side (I’ll follow with the spreadsheet calculations by EOD Thursday):
- Trailing-90d spend: ~$1.9M (hosted + dedicated). Top 3 drivers: long-context chat workloads, embeddings batch ops, and nightly evaluation jobs.
- Utilization: fleet average ~72% effective (production pools ~82%, staging/non-prod ~38%). There is ~14% burst headroom on our reserved pools given current autoscale settings; non-prod is overprovisioned by ~60% during business hours.
- Batching/cache baseline: median batch size = 9 tokens/req for generation paths, p50 prefix-reuse ~18%, overall cache hit-rate ~11%. Our modelling says: +20% batching (median -> 11) reduces per-token infra cost by ~8–9% but increases p99 latency on long-tail requests by ~18–22ms on average; raising cache TTL from 30s to 90s yields an additional ~6–7% token savings (varies by model) with negligible latency impact.
- Risk notes: larger batches hurt interactive UX for low-latency customers—need canary and per-route overrides. Cache TTL increases add stale-output risk for rapidly changing contexts (rare, but call out).

Proposed slides:
1) Runway chart (months until we hit reserved capacity threshold under baseline growth + 3 growth scenarios)
2) Heatmap: utilization by cluster and pool (prod/staging/non-prod)
3) Lever sensitivity table: % cost delta vs. p99 latency delta for batching and cache options

I’ll attach the scenario workbook (gpu_utilization_by_cluster_202701.pdf summary + CSV). Next actions for modeling:
- I’ll produce the baseline + two stress scenarios (10%/30% demand spikes) and a non-prod scale-down projection for the 15% reclaim ask.
- Need input from Product on acceptable p99 delta per customer tier (Lauren / Monica to define).

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 04 Feb 2027 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep — infra runway, GPU spend, batching/caching trade-offs

Thanks — good framework. A few leadership points to surface in the readout:
- OKR alignment: call out any infra levers that materially change our ability to hit the "response latency" objective for the quarter. If batching changes p99 by >15ms for a top-tier customer, we should not count that saving against the OKR unless we have a mitigation plan.
- Non-prod reclaim: I support a 15% reclaim of non-prod if the ops playbook (scheduled scale-down + quick rollback) is in place and runbook owners assigned. Please include the rollback SLAs and human runbook page link in the appendix.
- Customer-facing risk: include a short blurb on how we will communicate degradation risk to top-5 customers if we experiment with more aggressive batching. Monica, loop in CS language.

Also — Rishi, if runway shows <3 months under baseline growth, we should discuss an exec request for a short-term committed increase or a one-off deferred billing credit model for the largest customers to smooth cash flow.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Vivek —

Thanks for the heads-up and for pulling Atlas into the thread. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side that might also be useful to call out in the QBR:
1) If you reclaim 15% non-prod, what is the timeline for restoring that capacity if we see production impact? We need to understand typical ramp times and whether dedicated burst capacity is possible.
2) When you model cost savings from batching, are you looking at token-cost only, or end-to-end infra ($/hour GPU + token mix)? Our procurement team (cc’d) cares about the latter when evaluating committed spend.

Our procurement contact is also interested in options to reserve burst capacity (short-term add-on) while we move to a next-phase contract. Happy to discuss — we can join the QBR slot if useful.

Best,
Emily Wu
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasHealth
emily.wu@atlashealth.com
